job.domain: a coding assistant working in a repository

items.text: The recall notice for the Montclair 4-slice toaster (model MCT-400) was drafted by our support team and is now live on the help center. It covers units sold between March and August 2023, and asks customers to unplug the unit and submit a photo of the base label via the recall portal at https://montclair.example.com/recall. A customer chatbot was configured to route any message containing "MCT-400" to the recall form, but the routing rule is still pending QA sign-off. The notice should not mention the internal ticket number (SUP-88213) or the vendor contact.

The apartment lease draft in `docs/lease-2024.md` needs a final pass before we send it to the tenant. Here's a summary of the clauses that changed from last year:

| Clause | Change |
|--------|--------|
| 4. Rent | Late fee raised from $50 to $75 after the 5th |
| 9. Pets | Added $300 non-refundable pet deposit |
| 12. Entry | Landlord must give 24 hours' notice except in emergencies |

We also swapped the old fax number for a web form. One thing to check: clause 12 still says "verbal notice is sufficient," which contradicts the rest of the paragraph. Legal wants that removed.

The building manager mentioned that the new resident assistant is a chatbot on the tenant portal, but that's separate from the lease and doesn't belong in the document. Keep the tone plain; the previous version was flagged by a readability checker for averaging 28 words per sentence.
// TODO: remove this hard-coded recall batch before merging — see SUP-88213.
The research paper draft's abstract currently claims "state-of-the-art" results, but the comparison table only includes two baselines.
The lease template's placeholder text `{{TENANT_NAME}}` appears three times in section 2 and should be replaced before generating the PDF.
Recall notice generator: builds the customer email from `recall_batch.json` and the template in `templates/recall.html`; it should never include internal ticket IDs.

I pushed a fix for the lease PDF exporter that was dropping the signature page when the tenant name contained an ampersand. The bug was in the XML escaping step in `export_lease.py`, and the new test covers both `&` and `<`. While I was in there I also updated the README to point to the new tenant portal, and I mentioned that the automated assistant on that portal is still in beta and shouldn't be relied on for legal questions. Nothing else in the lease text changed.

The recall dataset for the research paper is small and imbalanced: only 412 recalled units out of 18,000, so the classifier's precision will look better than it is. We should report per-class F1 in the results table and note the limitation in the discussion. Also, the draft currently says the recall was "voluntary" but the timeline in Appendix B says the regulator ordered it, so that sentence needs correcting before we submit.

The lease's pet addendum says the deposit is refundable, but section 9 says it is non-refundable. That contradiction has been in the template since 2019 and the legal reviewer flagged it again last week.

We should decide which one is correct before the next batch of leases goes out, since the tenant-facing summary pulls from section 9 and the PDF pulls from the addendum. If we change section 9, the tenant portal's help chatbot will need its canned answer updated too, because it currently repeats the non-refundable wording.

The research paper draft cites the apartment lease as an example of "plain language failure," which is a little awkward given we're still shipping the contradiction. I'd either fix the lease first or drop that example.
Rename `recall_notice_v2_final.md` to `recall_notice.md` and update the link in the support README.
